failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor is a fixed recipe: it never moves the setpoints, so it cannot re-allocate production between the two lower tanks. Any disturbance that starves tank1 (draw-off from tank1, loss of pump-1 gain, or a downshift of gamma1) makes the h1 PI loop push v2, and therefore h3, up until the 0.75 m upper limit is violated and the pumps saturate; symmetric disturbances starve tank2 and push v1/h4. failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the window mass-balance disturbance estimator and the steady-state split solver; next, add a slow production-error correction (or a check for setpoint tracking) so that when a lower-tank PI loop saturates, the remaining production shortfall is recovered on the other lower tank.

self_check: Each call I integrate the four tank mass balances over the 50 s window to get the lumped lower-tank disturbances and the effective upper-tank drain coefficients, then solve the steady-state balances for the split of the production target between tank1 and tank2. The feasible split interval is bounded by the predicted h3/h4 levels (with margin) and the pump voltages (with the estimated effective gains), so when a disturbance pushes h3 toward 0.75 the supervisor moves production share to tank2 (and vice versa), and when the interval is empty it keeps the upper levels safe. Because those window estimates are exact at any steady state, the loop converges to a split that truly holds the binding constraint while Q stays on target, and it only moves the setpoints when the feasible interval excludes the current split.
proposed_change: Estimate the two lumped lower-tank disturbances and the effective upper-tank drain coefficients from the 50 s window mass balances, then choose the steady-state split of the production target between tank1 and tank2 whose predicted h3/h4 stay below the limit and whose pumps stay unsaturated, taking the split closest to the current one.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor assumes fixed split ratios gamma1=gamma2=0.20 and estimates disturbances from long-window (49 s) averages, so it mispredicts the effective flow split when a split-valve disturbance shifts gamma, and it lags oscillatory feed/split disturbances. This causes upper-level limit violations and large production off-target during sine disturbances.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate effective split ratios c1,c2 and unmeasured flows d1,d2 from recent telemetry via window regression, then choose the feasible production split for the target Q.

self_check: The supervisor estimates c1,c2,d1,d2,p1,p2 from the last 20 s, then computes the feasible interval of tank1 flow F1 that keeps h2 in band, h3/h4 below limit, and pumps unsaturated, and sets h1,h2 to the target-production curve clamped to that interval. If an upper level nears its limit, the feasible interval shifts to reduce that tank's inflow, forcing more production from the other tank while Q stays on target. If a pump saturates, its max flow caps the feasible interval, so the split moves to the other tank. The setpoints only move when the feasible interval or Q error requires it, minimizing travel.
proposed_change: Replace fixed gamma assumptions with online estimation of effective split ratios and unmeasured flows from the last 20 s, and recompute the feasible setpoint split that holds Q at target while respecting h2 band and upper-level limits.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The planner treats the h3/h4 limits only as steady-state feasibility bounds computed with nominal split gains, so under a combined pump-gain loss plus split shift the h3 excursion stays inside the LP interval and the setpoints never move; h3 then breaches 0.75 m for 138 s and h2 briefly leaves its band. The sinusoidal cases show the same open-loop weakness: the LP releases a setpoint pair once and never trims it as the upper levels drift.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Tighten the LP hi/lo bounds using the measured (not nominal) split gains and pump losses, so the feasibility interval itself shrinks when the plant deviates, instead of relying only on the added feedback trim.

self_check: The supervisor keeps production on target by splitting the target flow Q between the two lower tanks (F1 + F2 = Q) and converting that split into h1/h2 setpoints. When either upper level rises toward its limit, a predictive trim subtracts from the tank-1 share (or adds to it for h4) using the window's level slope and peak, which reduces the pump feeding that upper tank before the level crosses the limit. The trim is then re-clamped to the feasible interval defined by the h2 band, the u3/u4 caps and the pump voltage limits, so a saturating or gain-degraded pump cannot push the split past what the loop can hold. A 0.002 m deadband suppresses needless setpoint motion.
proposed_change: Add a predictive h3/h4 feedback trim on the production split on top of the existing LP: subtract from the tank-1 share when h3 is high or rising, add when h4 is high or rising, then re-clamp to the feasible interval. Tighten the planning margin on the h2 band and add a small setpoint deadband to cut travel.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor enforced only steady-state feasibility, so whenever a sine disturbance made pump2 (or pump1) run high to hold h1 (or h2), the lagging tank3/tank4 level transiently overshot: dev_combined_sine_0 held h3 at 0.78-0.81 m for 138 s with v2 near saturation, and the sine cases were dominated by unrejected production error (300+ L) because the split was never shifted to relieve the over-loaded side.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the exact steady-state feasibility clamp, but bound and dead-band the new predictive trim and re-check on held-out sine timings that it neither ratchets the split nor excites the level loops.

self_check: The feasible interval for the tank1 share of the target production is computed online from estimated split ratios, unmeasured feeds and pump gains, so the returned setpoints always imply h3/h4 at or below their limits and both pump voltages inside 1-12 V. On top of that clamp, a bounded dead-banded trim shifts production from tank1 to tank2 when h3 is heading above its limit (and the reverse for h4 or a high h2), using the windowed level slope times a lead time as a predictor so the pump voltage is reduced before the level peaks. Because the trim is capped per call and ignored below a 2.5 mm dead-band, the setpoints move only as far as the constraint margin requires and otherwise hold.
proposed_change: Replace the pure steady-state clamp with the same exact clamp plus a bounded, dead-banded predictive trim on the production split, driven by measured h3/h4/h2 and their windowed slopes. Keep setpoint motion rate-limited so the split is shifted only as far as the constraint margin needs, never more.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor's fixed split and lack of production feedback let h3 exceed 0.75 m during combined pump/split sine (138 s violation) and caused large Q deviations in feed/pump sines because it did not adjust setpoints to counter transient errors.
